claim:
Let \(d\gamma=(2\pi)^{-1}e^{-|x|^2/2}\,dx\) on \(\mathbb R^2\), and let \(T_\gamma(K)=\int_K u\,d\gamma\), where \((\Delta-x\cdot\nabla)u=-1\) in \(K\) and \(u=0\) on \(\partial K\). For every nonzero smooth \(2\pi\)-periodic function \(f\) satisfying \(f(\theta+\pi)=f(\theta)\) and \(\int_0^{2\pi}f(\theta)\,d\theta=0\), let \(K_\varepsilon\) have support function \(h_\varepsilon(\theta)=1+\varepsilon f(\theta)\) for sufficiently small \(|\varepsilon|\). Then \(\operatorname{Per}(K_\varepsilon)=2\pi\) exactly, and if \(f(\theta)=\sum_{k\ge2,\ k\ \mathrm{even}}(a_k\cos k\theta+b_k\sin k\theta)\), then
\[
\left.\frac{d^2}{d\varepsilon^2}T_\gamma(K_\varepsilon)\right|_{\varepsilon=0}
=\frac{\sqrt e-1}{2\sqrt e}\sum_{\substack{k\ge2\\ k\ \mathrm{even}}}\left[2-(\sqrt e-1)(k^2+2\lambda_k)\right](a_k^2+b_k^2)<0,
\]
where \(\lambda_k=F_k'(1)\) and
\[
F_k(r)=\frac{r^k\,{}_1F_1(k/2;k+1;r^2/2)}{{}_1F_1(k/2;k+1;1/2)}.
\]
Thus the unit disk is strictly second-order stable in every nontrivial smooth centrally symmetric Euclidean-perimeter-preserving support direction for Gaussian torsional rigidity. This is a local second-variation result only; it does not prove the global fixed-perimeter maximization problem.
integrity: The infinite-mode sign is proved analytically from the positive Kummer series and is not inferred from finite numerical tests. The standard smooth-domain differentiability step is stated explicitly. No independent audit has been performed.
scientific_limitations: Local second-directional variation at the planar unit disk only; smooth centrally symmetric support perturbations with exact Euclidean perimeter preservation. No global fixed-perimeter inequality, nonsmooth extension, higher-dimensional theorem, or neighborhood estimate is claimed.
title: Fixed-perimeter Gaussian torsion has a negative centrally symmetric Hessian at the disk
